findings: Equal-length rc.sysinit data replacement: drops the last two mount echo lines and appends a background Lua start after every mount; only the differing tail is stored.
The ROMFS inode checksum covers the unchanged 32-byte header/name and the filesystem checksum covers its unchanged first 512 bytes.

Physical boot acceptance FAILED: on a real Band 11, pinning corrupted flash and left the band in a boot loop (reported by the user, 2026-11-03). That was the /dev/bes_flash writer; the flash-HAL writer that replaced it is NOT device-tested, so Band 11 builds keep pinned start off except with CANOPUS_BOOT_DEVICE_TEST=1.

The erase block also holds 203 live bytes after the ROMFS: a driver file_operations table (0x0c330161, 0x0c3301bf, ...) and the gpiod_list_chips / spi_controller_create / bthci_register / bes_nand_* function names.

MTD up_progmem_eraseblock (0xc330dac) erases inside BASEPRI 0x80, then calls usleep(1) (udelay only in an interrupt or the idle task) before FTL programs the block, so other tasks run while it is blank; the 220-byte tail crosses a 512-byte BCH sector, so /dev/bes_flash rewrote the block twice.

The Supervisor now erases and programs the whole block with the BES flash HAL (symbols flash.app_flash_erase/program/flush) inside one BASEPRI 0x80 section, after a bits-only probe of the dropped echo line; block states are identified by block_crc32; unpinning clears 's' of the hook to '#' without an erase. Emulator evidence only (scripts/emu/boot_smoke.py).

boot.lua runs under the firmware's NSH `lua`, whose luaopen_screen keeps the interpreter's lua_State in a three-slot table (symbol lua.screen_lua_states) for screen_state_cb; only the app framework's lua_module_miwear_close clears a slot, so the state stays there after `lua` exits and every later screen change runs lua_getglobal on freed memory. Mirage q66 (emulator only): at the first screen change after boot.lua the miwear task faults (MemManage, MMFAR 0xd6a2, luaT_gettm under screen_state_cb) or hangs, and the band restarts. Since `b` runs `lua` at every start, also after boot.lua's attempt limit, a pinned Band 11 can loop like this indefinitely, which is a likely cause of the boot loop seen on the device. boot.lua (generated) now clears its own slot, matched against tostring(coroutine.running()), with one aligned `mw` write before anything else.
